# Getting Startedsvg image

Relevant source files

- [![svg image](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)README.md](https://github.com/ray0404/Contexter/blob/79ebf745/README.md)
- [![svg image](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)pyproject.toml](https://github.com/ray0404/Contexter/blob/79ebf745/pyproject.toml)

This page provides an introduction to installing and using Contexter, a Python command-line toolkit for packaging software projects into single text files (Markdown or HTML format). It covers the basic workflow, installation process, and command organization to help you begin working with the system.

For detailed installation instructions, see [Installation](/ray0404/Contexter/2.1-installation). For hands-on tutorials, see [Quick Start Guide](/ray0404/Contexter/2.2-quick-start-guide). For a complete list of all commands, see [Command Overview](/ray0404/Contexter/2.3-command-overview).

---

## Purpose and Scopesvg image

This section introduces the fundamental concepts needed to start using Contexter effectively:

- **Prerequisites**: System requirements and dependencies
- **Basic Workflow**: Understanding the core build→reconstruct cycle
- **Installation Overview**: How to install the package
- **Command Organization**: How the 12 CLI tools are structured
- **Next Steps**: Where to go after initial setup

This page does not cover:

- Detailed command syntax and options (see [Command Reference](/ray0404/Contexter/5-command-reference))
- Advanced workflows like patch management (see [Workflows](/ray0404/Contexter/4-workflows))
- Internal architecture details (see [Architecture](/ray0404/Contexter/6-architecture))

---

## Prerequisitessvg image

Contexter requires the following:

| Requirement | Version | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Python | ≥ 3.7 | Runtime environment |
| pip | Latest | Package installation |
| Virtual environment | Recommended | Isolated installation |

**External Dependencies** (automatically installed):

| Package | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `markdown` | Markdown processing |
| `Pygments` | Syntax highlighting |
| `markdownify` | HTML to Markdown conversion |
| `beautifulsoup4` | HTML parsing |
| `patch` | Diff/patch operations |

**Sources:** [![svg image](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)pyproject.toml15-29](https://github.com/ray0404/Contexter/blob/79ebf745/pyproject.toml#L15-L29) [![svg image](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)README.md39-60](https://github.com/ray0404/Contexter/blob/79ebf745/README.md#L39-L60)

## Basic Workflowsvg image

Contexter operates on a simple bidirectional workflow:

**Basic Workflow: Directory to Context File and Back**

### Core Cyclesvg image

1. **Build Phase**: A directory tree is scanned and aggregated into a single context file

   - Command: `buildcontext` (Markdown) or `buildcontexthtml` (HTML)
   - Output: Single text file containing all project files
2. **Distribution Phase**: The context file can be:

   - Shared with AI models for code review/generation
   - Stored as a text-based backup
   - Transferred between machines
   - Committed to version control
3. **Reconstruction Phase**: The context file is parsed and the original directory structure is recreated

   - Command: `reconstructor` (Markdown) or `reconstructorhtml` (HTML)
   - Output: Full directory tree with individual files

**Sources:** [![svg image](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)README.md3-7](https://github.com/ray0404/Contexter/blob/79ebf745/README.md#L3-L7) Diagram 2 from system overview

---

## Installation Overviewsvg image

Contexter is installed via `pip` from the project repository. Two installation modes are available:

### Standard Installationsvg image

This installs Contexter and its dependencies in the current Python environment. The package registers 12 CLI commands as entry points.

### Editable Installation (Development)svg image

This creates symlinks to the source code, allowing modifications to be immediately reflected without reinstallation. Recommended for contributors and users who want to customize behavior.

### Entry Point Registrationsvg image

Both installation modes register CLI commands via `setup.py` entry points. Each command maps to a `main()` function in its corresponding module:

**CLI Command Registration Mapping**

After installation, all 12 commands become available globally in your shell environment.

**Verification**: Run `buildcontext --help` to confirm successful installation.

**Sources:** [![svg image](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)README.md39-60](https://github.com/ray0404/Contexter/blob/79ebf745/README.md#L39-L60) [![svg image](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)pyproject.toml1-33](https://github.com/ray0404/Contexter/blob/79ebf745/pyproject.toml#L1-L33) Diagram 3 from system overview

For complete installation details including troubleshooting, see [Installation](/ray0404/Contexter/2.1-installation).

---

## Command Organizationsvg image

Contexter provides 12 CLI commands organized into four functional categories:

### Command Categoriessvg image

| Category | Commands | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Building** | `buildcontext` `buildcontexthtml` | Create context files from directories |
| **Reconstruction** | `reconstructor` `reconstructorhtml` | Rebuild directories from context files |
| **Updates** | `updatecontext` `updater` `smartupdate` `updatecontexthtml` `updaterhtml` | Generate and apply patches for version management |
| **Utilities** | `sanitizecontext` `md2html` `html2md` | Fix AI output, convert between formats |

### Format Dualitysvg image

Most operations support both Markdown and HTML formats with parallel command sets:

| Operation | Markdown Command | HTML Command |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Build | `buildcontext` | `buildcontexthtml` |
| Reconstruct | `reconstructor` | `reconstructorhtml` |
| Update Patch | `updatecontext` | `updatecontexthtml` |
| Apply Patch | `updater` | `updaterhtml` |

**Format Conversion**: Use `md2html` and `html2md` to convert context files between formats.

**Sources:** [![svg image](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)README.md20-36](https://github.com/ray0404/Contexter/blob/79ebf745/README.md#L20-L36) Diagram 1 from system overview

---

## Command Implementation Structuresvg image

Each CLI command is implemented as a thin wrapper around an implementation module:

**Command to Module Mapping**

**Key Points**:

- Each CLI command has exactly one corresponding implementation module
- All modules share common functionality through `contexter_utils.py`
- Commands can be invoked programmatically by importing the module and calling `main()`

For a complete list of commands with descriptions, see [Command Overview](/ray0404/Contexter/2.3-command-overview). For detailed command syntax and options, see [Command Reference](/ray0404/Contexter/5-command-reference).

**Sources:** [![svg image](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)README.md20-36](https://github.com/ray0404/Contexter/blob/79ebf745/README.md#L20-L36) Diagram 3 from system overview

## Your First Commandssvg image

### Example 1: Package a Projectsvg image

This scans `/path/to/project`, aggregates all non-excluded files, and writes them to `my_project.md` as a single Markdown file.

### Example 2: Reconstruct a Projectsvg image

This parses `my_project.md`, extracts the directory structure and file contents, and recreates the project in `./restored_project`.

### Example 3: AI Workflow (New in v2.0.0)svg image

The `sanitizecontext` command detects and fixes missing code fences (```` ``` ````) commonly omitted by AI models, making the output compatible with `reconstructor`.
